/-!
# Erdős Problem 57

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/57](https://www.erdosproblems.com/57)
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [LiMo20] Liu, Hong and Montgomery, Richard, *A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem*.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos57

/--
If $G$ is a graph with infinite chromatic number and $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ are lengths of the odd
cycles of $G$ then $\sum \frac{1}{a_i} = \infty$.

Conjectured by Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa66], and solved by Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20].

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) states the conclusion as
`¬ Summable (oddCycleReciprocal G)`, where `oddCycleReciprocal G n` is `n⁻¹` if `n` is an odd
cycle length of `G` and `0` otherwise; this is the indicator form of the sum below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos57.lean#L11124"]
theorem erdos_57 :
    ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ →
      ¬ Summable (fun (a : G.oddCycleLengths) ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos57

findings.description: The docstring at line 39 cites [ErHa66] as the source of the odd-cycle reciprocal-divergence conjecture. Problem 7.8 of that paper concerns the set of all cycle lengths, without restricting to odd lengths. The odd-cycle conjecture is stated in Erdős's 1981 paper. This is a bibliographic slip only: the Lean theorem correctly states Erdős Problem 57.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Hajnal, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems (1966), Problem 7.8, p. 78, defines N as the integers i for which the graph contains a circuit of length i (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1966-07.pdf). Erdős, Problems and results in graph theory (1981), §5, p. 338, states the infinite-chromatic conjecture with reciprocals 1/(2r+1), where 2r+1 runs through the odd circuit lengths (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-20.pdf). Liu–Montgomery explicitly distinguish the 1966 all-cycle question in §1.1 from the odd-cycle question posed in 1981 in §1.2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.15802). The problem website also repeats the 1966 attribution; this finding is based on the primary papers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [Er81]: Erdős, P., Problems and results in graph theory, The theory and applications of graphs (Kalamazoo, MI, 1980), 331–341 (1981), and replace [ErHa66] in the conjecture-attribution sentence with [Er81]. Retain [ErHa66] only if explaining the earlier all-cycle problem. No change to the Lean statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: The source writes an increasing enumeration of distinct odd cycle lengths and asserts that its reciprocal series equals infinity. Lean instead asserts nonsummability of the real-valued function on the subtype G.oddCycleLengths. The linked formal proof uses a zero-extended function on all natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The subtype indexes each odd cycle length exactly once, and every such length is at least 3, so all reciprocals are positive. Summability is invariant under a bijective enumeration and is equivalent to summability of the zero-extended indicator function. For this nonnegative real sequence, nonsummability is equivalent to its partial sums tending to +infinity. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved the indicator equivalence, the divergence equivalence, the enumeration equivalence, and the exact bridge to copies of the external proof's definitions; these proofs have no sorry dependencies.

review.notes: The mathematical statement is faithful. Verified that chromaticNumber = ⊤ means absence of every finite proper coloring, not a restriction to a particular infinite cardinal. Lean experiments exclude lengths 0, 1, and 2; check empty and finite graphs; exhibit the infinite complete graph as a satisfiable hypothesis; and compute that a triangle is a cycle while nil and a two-edge backtrack are not. Both scratch.lean and boundaries.lean compile successfully. The solved/formal-proof status agrees with the source. The external proof's statement and definitions were inspected and bridged, but its entire dependency project was not rebuilt. The reviewed file remains byte-for-byte equal to the committed version.
